title: Cortical and meningeal neuroimmune interactions contribute to the generation of migraine headaches
title_zh: 皮层和脑膜神经免疫相互作用对偏头痛头痛发生的贡献
abstract: Abstract Migraine is a prevalent disorder that ranks as the second leading cause of disability among all diseases. Recent advancements have significantly enhanced our comprehension of its underlying pathophysiology. Growing evidence highlights complex neuroimmune signaling networks—particularly interactions between meningeal nociceptors and resident immune cells—as key contributors to headache generation. The clinical success of anti–calcitonin gene–related peptide (CGRP) antibodies underscores the importance of intercellular communication between the dural nociceptive nerves and adjacent resident immune cells such as macrophages in migraine headache. Notably, the intercellular inflammatory interplay is not confined to the meninges. Disturbances within the brain parenchyma potentially act as initiating triggers, as suggested by the presence of aura and premonitory symptoms preceding the headache. Recent experimental discoveries indicate that neuronal stress triggers an inflammatory signaling cascade that, through interactions with astrocytes and microglia, propagates to the meninges, ultimately inducing meningeal neurogenic inflammation and headache. This model is supported by converging experimental evidence and human imaging studies employing PET and quantitative MRI, which document the presence of changes compatible with inflammatory activity within the brain parenchyma and overlying meninges of patients with migraine with aura. Genetic studies identifying several inflammation-related genes and pathways as risk factors for migraine further corroborate this concept. Furthermore, cell-specific transcriptomic analyses of mouse brains have revealed astrocyte-selective activation of nuclear factor kappa B –regulated inflammatory transcriptional pathways after cortical spreading depolarization, the neurophysiological correlate of migraine aura. Owing to their extensive interface with the cerebrospinal fluid, astrocytes are uniquely positioned to release inflammatory mediators to activate meningeal nociceptors and immune cells. Insights from pain research suggest that neuroimmune interactions may be responsible for the widespread parenchymal increases in 18 kDa translocator protein (TSPO) PET signals observed in migraine with aura patients. This discovery also identifies TSPO as a potential player in migraine pathophysiology and novel drug target. In this review, by integrating cellular and molecular findings from peripheral pain and inflammation research, we examine the dynamic interactions between neurons and glia, as well as between meningeal nociceptors and immune cells in the context of migraine headache. This perspective provides a conceptual framework for understanding how nociceptors and glial cells coordinate to signal non-homeostatic brain states—initiating protective, tightly regulated responses without progressing to overt neuroinflammatory disease and provides novel insight into the findings of PET studies involving TSPO.
abstract_zh: 摘要 偏头痛是一种普遍的疾病，在所有疾病中按致残原因排列第二位。近年来的进展显著增强了我们对其潜在病理生理学的认识。越来越多的证据突出了复杂的神经免疫信号网络，特别是脑膜伤害感受器与驻留免疫细胞之间的相互作用，作为头痛发生的关键贡献因素。抗降钙素基因相关肽（CGRP）抗体的临床成功凸显了硬膜伤害感受性神经与相邻驻留免疫细胞（如巨噬细胞）之间的细胞间通讯在偏头痛中的重要性。值得注意的是，这种细胞间炎症相互作用并不局限于脑膜。脑实质内的紊乱可能充当诱发因素，如先兆和前驱症状在头痛前出现所提示的那样。最近的实验发现表明，神经元应激会引发炎症信号级联反应，通过与星形胶质细胞和小胶质细胞的相互作用传播至脑膜，最终诱发脑膜神经源性炎症和头痛。该模型得到汇聚实验证据和采用PET及定量MRI的人类成像研究的支持，这些研究记录了偏头痛伴先兆患者脑实质及其覆盖脑膜中与炎症活动相容的改变。确定多个炎症相关基因和通路作为偏头痛风险因素的遗传研究进一步证实了这一概念。此外，小鼠大脑的细胞特异性转录组分析揭示了皮质扩散性去极化（偏头痛先兆的神经生理学相关物）后星形胶质细胞选择性激活核因子κB调控的炎症转录通路。由于星形胶质细胞与脑脊液具有广泛的界面，它能独特地释放炎症介质以激活脑膜伤害感受器和免疫细胞。疼痛研究的洞见提示，神经免疫相互作用可能导致偏头痛伴先兆患者中广泛的脑实质18 kDa转位蛋白（TSPO）PET信号增加。这一发现还确定TSPO作为偏头痛病理生理学的潜在参与者和新的药物靶点。在本综述中，通过整合外周疼痛和炎症研究的细胞与分子发现，我们考察了在偏头痛背景下神经元与胶质细胞、以及脑膜伤害感受器与免疫细胞之间的动态相互作用。这一视角为理解伤害感受器和胶质细胞如何协调发出非稳态脑状态的信号提供了概念框架——发起受保护、受严格调控的反应而不发展为显性神经炎症性疾病，并对涉及TSPO的PET研究结果提供了新的洞察。
